title: Rank-one Thom isomorphism
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a
vector bundle of constant
rank one, with the zero section $z:B\hookrightarrow E$. The zero
section is an effective Cartier divisor of $E$ (the zero scheme of the
tautological section of $\pi^*E$); let

$$
\operatorname{thom}(E):z_*\Lambda_B\longrightarrow\Lambda_E(1)[2]
$$

be its class $\operatorname{cl}_{z(B)}$ of [lem-pur-divisor-class],
and put

$$
\tau_E:=
R\pi_!\operatorname{thom}(E):
\Lambda_B\longrightarrow R\pi_!\Lambda_E(1)[2].
$$

Then $\tau_E$ is an isomorphism, compatible with base change. Its
inverse $\operatorname{tr}_\pi$ is the *rank-one vector-bundle
trace*. In particular

$$
R\pi_!\Lambda_E\;\cong\;\Lambda_B(-1)[-2].
$$

proof.text: Work at the arbitrary finite level $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. By [lem-pur-line-zero-class-etale-realization], the zero divisor is Cartier, its specified class is $c_{z(B),A}$, and $R\pi_!z_*A_B=A_B$ canonically. Hence $\tau_E=R\pi_!c_{z(B),A}$ is the actual bounded-below etale-origin morphism supplied there, with the prescribed pro-etale twist.

source.place: Step 1: global class and induced map

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-line-zero-class-exchange]. It gives compatibility of $\tau_E$ with the specified compact-support exchange for every base change, with identity source component. At a geometric point $\bar b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$, choose a basis of the fibre line. The same lemma identifies its stalk morphism with the realization of the compact image $\tau_X^e$ of the origin class on $X=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$, with ordinary etale twist $L=\mu_{\ell^n}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes A$.

source.place: Step 3 and Step 2: normalized base change and fibres

proof.text: Take $N=\ell^n$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ (Noetherian, $N$ invertible), $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ with $q:P\to S$, $j:X\hookrightarrow P$, and $C$, $a$, $h$ of [lem-pur-origin-class-projective-comparison], which gives $a\tau_X^e=h$. By [def-amb-p1-trace], $t_q=\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1}$ for the decomposition $b_q$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], and $t_qh=1_A$. By [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] with $d=1$, the counit $t_{p_1}$ at $A_S$ is an isomorphism; by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] it is $\epsilon_{q,A_S}\circ Rq_*(\epsilon^j)$, that is $\epsilon_{q,A_S}\circ a$ after the unit isomorphism $q^*A_S\otimes^L_AL_P\cong L_P$. At $K=A_S$ the projection map of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] is the identity under the unit isomorphisms (the symmetry has sign $+1$ in degree zero, and $\mathrm{PF}$ is adjoint to the counit $q^*Rq_*M\to M$), so $\epsilon_{q,A_S}=t_q$. Hence $\beta:=t_qa:C\to A$ is an isomorphism and $\beta\tau_X^e=t_qh=1_A$. Thus $\tau_X^e=\beta^{-1}$ is invertible, with coefficient $+1$.

Every geometric stalk of $\tau_E$ is consequently an isomorphism in every degree. Step 1 supplied an etale representative of the morphism itself, so clause 3 of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative] applies and proves $\tau_E$ invertible. Define $\operatorname{tr}_\pi=\tau_E^{-1}$; inverting the exchange identity from Step 2 gives its base-change compatibility.

Finally [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] applies with $K=A_E$ and $L=A_B(1)$: both are bounded constructible and $L$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], with its prescribed pro-etale realization as in [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. It identifies
$$R\pi_!A_E(1)[2]\cong(R\pi_!A_E)\otimes_A^L A_B(1)[2].$$
Tensor with $A_B(-1)[-2]$. The evaluation and twist-pullback identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], realized with the same finite twist, cancel $A_B(1)$, giving $R\pi_!A_E\cong A_B(-1)[-2]$.
